title: {{product}} Help Center
subtitle: Comprehensive manuals and security documentation for {{product}}.

tasks.title: Common task questions
tasks.fullLink: A full link includes everything after the #. Copy the complete link so the recipient's browser has the decryption key.
tasks.credentials: Your account PIN is never something to send to a recipient. A link password, sender password, and your vault PIN are different credentials.
tasks.failedDownload: If the link is complete and still active, retry the download. A server or network failure does not mean the link key is missing.
tasks.revokeLimits: Revoking a link stops future access. It cannot erase a file a recipient already downloaded.
tasks.partialUpload: If some files fail, retry only the failed files after the page identifies which uploads were confirmed.
tasks.senderPassword: A File Request password protects that sender journey. It is not the owner's account password or vault PIN.
tasks.dropRecovery: Secure Drop keeps server-side recovery material for authorized owner recovery. Senders still never need the owner's account password or vault PIN.
tasks.pinPurpose: Your vault PIN unlocks supported owner and account-sharing keys in your browser. Never give it to another person.
tasks.recoveryLimit: Account recovery requires enough configured custodians. It cannot promise recovery when the required key shares are unavailable. Files protected by an earlier PIN or file password still need that original credential.

getting_started.title: Getting Started with {{product}}
paragraphs: Welcome to {{product}}. Files are encrypted in your browser before upload, and each supported access path has an explicit key and authorization contract.
Account vault and sharing keys are unlocked in authorized browsers. Secure Drop is a separate intake path with server-side recovery material for authorized owner recovery.
To begin, explore your Dashboard. This is your primary workspace where you can manage your Vault, track your active Drop Portals, and audit recent file interactions.

callout.title: Know the access path
callout.text: File contents are encrypted before upload. Use the access history and credential prompt to confirm which account, link, or Secure Drop path applies.

vault_pin.title: Your Vault PIN and account recovery
paragraphs: Your Vault is the secure repository for your personal encrypted files. A 4-digit vault PIN can unlock supported owner and account-sharing keys after onboarding.
This PIN is used to locally derive your master encryption keys. It is never transmitted to or stored on our servers in plaintext.
When you log in from a new device or after your session expires, you will be prompted to enter this PIN to unlock your local keychain.
bulletPoints: Never share your PIN with anyone, including administrators.
Store your PIN in a secure password manager.
Account recovery can restore eligible account key material after enough configured custodians approve it, but it does not reveal your old PIN.

callout.title: Original credentials can still be required
callout.text: Files encrypted with an earlier PIN or file password still require that original credential. A recovered account key or new PIN does not re-encrypt those files.

uploads_shares.title: Uploads & Secure Sharing
paragraphs: Uploading files to {{product}} is seamless. Simply drag and drop files or folders into your Vault. The encryption process happens instantly in memory before the upload begins.
To collaborate externally without compromising security, you can generate a 'Share Link'. When you create a Share Link, the decryption key is embedded in the URL fragment (the part after the `#`).
Because URL fragments are never sent to the server by the browser, the server routes the encrypted file to the recipient, and the recipient's browser uses the fragment key to decrypt it locally.
bulletPoints: Share Links can be set to expire after a specific number of days.
You can instantly revoke any active Share Link from the Access Center.
The server tracks link access analytics (IP, timestamp) for your audit log without seeing the file content.

callout.title: Secure Transmission
callout.text: Even if the transmission is intercepted, the payload remains protected by AES-256-GCM. Only the recipient with the full URL containing the fragment key can decrypt the payload.

drop_portals.title: Drop Portals & File Requests
paragraphs: Drop Portals allow you to securely collect files from external parties who do not have a {{product}} account. When you create a Drop Portal, you generate a public, branded upload page.

External senders upload files encrypted in their browser for the intended owner. Secure Drop also keeps server-side recovery material for authorized owner recovery; this exception is separate from ordinary account vault access.
You can configure Drop Portals with required-document checklists, expiration dates, and custom instructions. This is ideal for secure document intake, KYC processes, and confidential reporting.

workspaces.title: Workspaces & Groups
paragraphs: For internal enterprise collaboration, {{product}} utilizes Workspaces and Groups. Groups allow you to share encrypted files with multiple users simultaneously without managing individual share links.
When you share a file with a Group, your browser encrypts the file's symmetric key using the public RSA keys of all current Group members.

Removing a member stops future group sharing. Review direct file grants and earlier downloads separately because group removal cannot erase a recipient copy or silently revoke an independent direct grant.

user_management.title: User Management (Admin)
paragraphs: As a system administrator, you have the authority to manage organizational access via the Settings dashboard. This includes provisioning new users, managing role assignments, and revoking access.

Deactivating a user stops future authentication. Review group membership, direct file grants, active links, and prior downloads separately; account deactivation cannot erase a copy already downloaded.
Administrators can also manage default storage quotas and organizational constraints.
bulletPoints: Ensure you verify the identity of users before assigning Admin roles.
Deactivated users retain their historical audit logs for compliance.

callout.title: Cryptographic Isolation
callout.text: Administrators manage access but cannot bypass encryption. You cannot view the plaintext contents of your users' Vaults.

agent_keys.title: Agent API Keys (Admin)
paragraphs: Agent API Keys allow you to integrate {{product}} with external systems, AI agents, and automation workflows. These keys provide programmatic access to the platform's stable REST API.
When generating an Agent API Key, you must adhere to the principle of least privilege by scoping the key to specific operations (e.g., `files:list`, `activity:read`).
Keys are fully revocable. The server only stores a cryptographic hash of the key. The plaintext key is shown only once at creation time.
bulletPoints: Use the built-in Filemon Operator to test your keys interactively.
Monitor key usage and last-seen timestamps via the Audit Log.
Rotate keys periodically to adhere to internal security protocols.

audit_logs.title: Audit Logs & Compliance (Admin)
paragraphs: The Audit Log provides a chronological record for supported security and administrative events. An empty or unavailable result is not proof that no activity occurred.
Recorded events can include user authentication, file uploads, share-link creation, and Agent API Key use. Confirm the event type and freshness shown before relying on it.
Administrators can filter the audit log by date, actor, resource type, and action, and export the data as CSV or JSON for integration with external SIEM tools.

system_settings.title: System Settings (Admin)
paragraphs: Global configuration settings dictate the security posture of the {{product}} deployment. Administrators can adjust retention policies, enforce session timeouts, and configure stale-link auto-expiry rules.
Use the Audit Log to confirm whether a supported setting change was recorded. Ensure any changes align with your organization's internal data governance and compliance mandates.
